title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, runbooks, roadmap, and retrospective (Q1 2027)
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Overview

This page consolidates our platform engineering guidance for systems & services ownership, common how-tos, dashboards and alerting, operational runbooks, the near-term roadmap, and a short retrospective for Q4 2026 — Q1 2027. The goal is a single living reference for oncall, runbook authors, and new platform team members.

Table of contents
1. Scope and ownership
2. Systems & services inventory (high-level)
3. How-tos (fast tasks)
4. Dashboards & alerts (key panels and thresholds)
5. Incident runbooks (playbooks)
6. Retrospective & action items
7. Roadmap (next 3 quarters)
8. Team wiki pointers and onboarding checklist

1) Scope and ownership

- Scope: this document covers services owned by the Platform Systems & Services subteam (see inventory below). It excludes model-serving GPU runtime internals (eng-serving-runtime), security controls (security-and-compliance), and customer-managed Private deployments (eng-private-deployments) except where integration points exist.
- Primary owners: Platform Systems & Services (platform infra, routing, observability pipelines).
- Pager/Oncall: platform-sre team owns first response for platform control-plane incidents. Model-serving incidents are routed to eng-serving-runtime after initial triage.
- SLAs / SLOs that platform tracks:
  - Control plane availability (write/read): 99.95% monthly
  - API request latency (control-plane ops): p95 < 180ms, p99 < 350ms
  - Alerting pipeline freshness: 95% of alerts delivered within 30s

2) Systems & services inventory (high-level)

- service: platform-api (REST control plane) | owner: Platform API team | contact: @marco | criticality: P0
- service: router (smart routing & fallback) | owner: Routing team | contact: @lina | criticality: P0
- service: cache-proxy (prefix/KV cache) | owner: Caching team | contact: @ethan | criticality: P1
- service: metrics-collector (observability ingestion) | owner: Observability | contact: @sofia | criticality: P1
- service: alert-dispatcher (pager & webhook forwarder) | owner: Alerting | contact: @dylan | criticality: P1
- infra: kubernetes-cluster-platform | owner: infra-k8s | contact: @olga | criticality: P0

Include the active runbook link in our team wiki for each service (see "Team wiki pointers").

3) How-tos (fast tasks)

- Deploy a hotfix to platform-api (canary -> roll):
  1. Create branch and CI run; confirm green e2e and smoke tests.
  2. Upload image to registry: `registry.redwood-inference/internal/platform-api:<sha>`
  3. Create canary release using our release tool: `./release-tool promote --service platform-api --image <sha> --strategy canary --pct 10`
  4. Monitor canary panels for 15 minutes; if no error rate increase and latency stable, escalate to 50% then 100%.
  5. If error rate > 0.5% or p95 latency +30% vs baseline, rollback: `./release-tool rollback --service platform-api --to previous`.

- Rotate service account keys (short):
  1. Create new KMS-protected key in vault.
  2. Deploy updated secret via `kubectl create secret generic` to staging, then prod during maintenance window.
  3. Verify consumers by checking success logs for 5m.

- Add dashboard panel (Prometheus + Grafana):
  1. Create panel JSON in `dashboards/` repo and run `make validate-dashboard`.
  2. Submit PR, include panel description and owner.
  3. On merge, alerting-engine will pick up new metrics if a matching alert rule is created.

4) Dashboards & alerts (key panels and thresholds)

Primary dashboards (links in team wiki):
- Platform Overview (team-level): service availability, global error rate, total requests per second, control-plane latency p50/p95/p99.
- Router Health: per-region routing success rate, fallback count per minute, route latency.
- Cache Observability: hit rate, eviction rate, average TTL, backend latency.
- Cluster Health: node CPU %, GPU utilization (where applicable), pod restart rate, node NotReady count.
- Alerting & Oncall: current open alerts, mean time to acknowledge, alert-to-pager ratio.

Key alert rules (examples):
- Control plane error rate high:
  - condition: 5m error rate > 0.5% for platform-api (all environments)
  - severity: sev1
  - notify: platform-oncall PagerDuty, #platform-alerts Slack channel
- Router fallback surge:
  - condition: fallback_count_rate > 50/min over 5m or 10x baseline
  - severity: sev1
  - runbook: see Router fallback runbook below
- Cache degraded (hit-rate drop):
  - condition: cache_hit_rate drops by >20% relative to 1h baseline for 10m
  - severity: sev2
  - mitigation: reduce eviction, scale cache-proxy, inspect backend latency
- Cluster node pressure:
  - condition: aggregate node CPU >85% for 10m OR pod eviction rate >2/min
  - severity: sev1/sev2 depending on impact
- Observability ingestion lag:
  - condition: alert pipeline delivery latency median > 60s for 5m
  - severity: sev2

Alert routing: all sev1 go to PagerDuty primary for Platform SRE. Sev2 open Slack thread and to next-oncall. Pager escalation policy is defined in our SRE handbook.

5) Incident runbooks (playbooks)

A. Router fallback surge (typical sev1)
Steps (first 30 minutes):
1. Acknowledge pager and open incident channel (#inc-platform-XXXX).
2. Run quick health checks:
   - `kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=router`
   - `kubectl -n platform logs deployment/router --since=5m | tail -n 200`
   - `curl -sS "https://router.internal/health" | jq .`
3. Check fallback metrics: Grafana panel + `promql`:
   - `sum(rate(router_fallback_count[5m])) by (region)`
4. If the fallback spike is from a single region, flip routing to secondary region (if allowed):
   - Run `./routerctl set-weight --region us-west-2 --weight 0.0` (temporary)
   - Monitor customer impact for 5 minutes.
5. If the spike is due to upstream timeouts, increase router timeouts or enable short-circuiting to cached model variants.
6. If root cause is a downstream service (platform-api/cache-proxy), escalate to that service owner and follow their runbook.
7. Post-incident: collect traces, attach to incident, and set a 7-day follow-up action for regression test.

B. Control plane error-rate increase (sev1)
Checklist:
1. Verify deploy activity in the last 30 minutes: `git log --since="30 minutes" --pretty=oneline` in release repo.
2. If a release is implicated, rollback to previous stable image.
3. If not a release, check DB connectivity and rate limits: `kubectl logs platform-api -c api | grep -E "(db|quota|ratelimit)"`
4. Temporary mitigation: enable read-only mode if writes are failing (use `./maintenance-mode enable --service platform-api --reason "investigation"`).
5. Communicate to stakeholders via incident channel and update status page.

Post-incident: run RCA using the standard template — include timelines, contributing factors, and three concrete mitigations with owners.

6) Retrospective (Q4 2026 — Q1 2027)

Summary: we observed three sev1 incidents in Q4 2026 impacting control-plane availability and router fallback surges tied to simultaneous customer traffic peaks and a misconfigured cache eviction policy. Overall uptime met SLA but margins narrowed during peak tests.

Key contributing factors:
- Insufficient routing isolation for high-variance tenant traffic.
- Cache eviction policy (default LRU with small TTL) caused backend amplification under load.
- Alert noise from low-signal metrics delayed pagers for the primary incident by ~4 minutes.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Introduce per-tenant routing weight caps and simulated chaos tests (owner: Routing team / @lina; due: 2027-03-31).
- Rework cache eviction policy to adaptive TTL and add a small hot-key protection layer (owner: Caching team / @ethan; due: 2027-02-28).
- Trim and retune alert rules; add runbook quick-links in alert payloads (owner: Observability / @sofia; due: 2027-02-15).
- Add integration test that simulates 10x baseline traffic from a synthetic tenant (owner: Platform QA / @nina; due: 2027-04-15).

7) Roadmap (next 3 quarters)

Q2 2027 (near-term)
- Adaptive cache policies + hot-key protection (priority).
- Per-tenant routing caps and improved traffic simulation.
- Alert consolidation and oncall playbook improvements.

Q3 2027
- Automated canary promotion with rollback heuristics (reduce human intervention).
- Observability: add distributed trace sampling that preserves tail latency traces.
- Provide public runbook templates for customer-facing Private deployments.

Q4 2027
- Fleet autoscaling improvements: predictive scaling using request forecasting model.
- Cross-region failover drills and documented RTO targets.

Milestones and dependencies: adaptive cache requires schema changes to cache-metadata; canary automation depends on release-tool v2.0 API. See related tasks in JIRA EPIC: PLAT-1823.

8) Team wiki pointers and onboarding checklist

- Required reading for new platform hires:
  - Platform playbook (core runbooks and oncall) — link: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-playbook-2026.json
  - Router architecture overview — link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/router-architecture (internal)
  - Observability standards — link: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards

- Onboarding checklist (first 30 days):
  1. Read playbook and practice the Router fallback runbook in a game-day.
  2. Walkthrough of release flow and perform a staging canary.
  3. Add yourself to PagerDuty schedule and validate mobile notifications.
  4. Subscribe to platform dashboards and join #platform-alerts Slack channel.

Appendix: useful commands & queries
- List platform pods: `kubectl -n platform get pods -l team=platform -o wide`
- Router fallback rate (PromQL): `sum(rate(router_fallback_count[5m])) by (region)`
- Platform API p95 latency (PromQL): `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="platform-api"}[5m])) by (le))`

Document maintenance
- Owner: Priya Kapoor (Platform Systems & Services).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any sev1 incident.
- To propose changes: submit PR to `confluence/docs` repo and add reviewers from the reviewers list above.
